analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (head lines 170-174). It adds a statement that a lifecycle drain on a provider with no registered session completes without a coordinator acknowledgement once accepted work and local response writes finish, citing ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift `performLifecycleDrain`. No executable code is in this batch, so no control was changed here. Cross-checked against TB-002, TB-011, T-053 and A-016. The doc says a drain acknowledgement is not a bearer credential or serving permission, and the new sentence concerns only the case where no session exists, so no coordinator-side authorization is skipped. Reconnect admission still goes through a fresh registration and authorization on a new connection. I found no interaction that weakens final-handoff authorization, revocation or endpoint binding.

Open question for the next pass: the underlying Swift change is not in this batch. Reviewers should confirm that `performLifecycleDrain` treats 'no registered session' strictly. A stale or half-torn-down session must not be mistaken for no session, because that would let the provider skip the barrier while the coordinator still has accepted work and billing in flight (T-010, billing settlement). The docs elsewhere say that if a barrier may have permanently fenced the old session, admission stays closed until a confirmed drain and reconnect. Whether the code honors this cannot be established from the documentation alone. This is an unverified contract, not a finding. Nothing in the patch changes secrets, keys, attestation, encryption or the wire format.
